newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end higher on Dow rise, poll hopes.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end higher on Dow rise, poll hopes.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed higher on Friday, propped up psychologically by a new record high on Wall Street overnight as well as hopes that Japan's general election on Sunday will produce a stable government capable of executing policies to help the economy, brokers said.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 ended 188.56 points or 0.88 percent higher at 21,612.30. Its December futures gained 200 to end at 21,700.
"Institutional investors were buying in anticipation of the elections," said Daiichi Securities analyst Akishige Ishikura. "Futures-linked trade also made the market hum with activity."

Advancing issues overwhelmed declining issues, 879 to 205 with 144 unchanged. On a sector basis, the main losers were railway/bus and precision instruments. The gainers were air transportation, ship building, oil, sea transportation and ceramics.

Media reports earlier this week quoted a senior LDP member of parliament as saying a five trillion yen supplementary budget should be considered by the end of the calendar year, prompting investors to buy issues related to public expenditure, such as construction companies and real estate developers.

Construction company Taisei Corp was up 11 yen at 725 yen, in volume of 1.358 million shares. Kajima Corp was up 20 yen at 1,060 yen. Tobishima Corp was 30 yen higher at 446 yen, inspired by a new restructuring plan.

Media reports that an advisory panel to the prime minister was likely to propose a review of the land taxation system by the end of November gave realtors a further boost. A National Land Agency official told Reuters on Friday that no proposal had been unveiled yet and the panel was likely to announce a proposal on new land policy in late November to early December.
Mitsui Fudosan Co, the sixth most heavily traded issue with 5.095 million shares changing hands, and Mitsubishi Estate both added 10 yen to close at 1,500 yen and 1,530 yen respectively.
Takeda Chemical Industries closed at a year high of 2,060 yen after rising as much as 30 yen to 2,060 yen.
Brokers said Takeda, along with Sankyo Co Ltd, which rose 70 yen to 2,820 yen, is a major pharmaceutical issue which is included in most institutional investor portfolios.
Canon Inc closed at its life high of 2,330 after rising 40 yen to 2,330 yen. -- M.Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk
